title.rendered: Crawford County Once Again Under a Burn Ban

content.rendered: (Undated) — Crawford County is once again under a Burn Ban. Crawford County Sheriff, Bill Rutan, announced yesterday that due to continued high temperatures and lack of rain, he and local fire officials have decided to reinstate the county-wide burn ban effective immediately. He reminds the public that no open burning is allowed, with the exception of small contained fires for cooking purposes. The ban will continue until further notice.

(Undated) – Crawford County authorities have lifted the recent burn ban. According to Crawford County Sheriff, Bill Rutan, due to the rainfall we have received over the last few days in our area, he, along with fire officials countywide, has decided to lift the recent burn ban at this time throughout Crawford County. However, they advise the public to be cautious in burning, as fires can quickly get out of hand. Here at the Classic Hits studio, we’ve recorded 2.30 inches of rain, the majority of which fell from Tuesday into Wednesday. WTAY/WTYE continues to be an official weather recording and reporting station for the National Weather Service.

(Undated) — Relief from the current burn ban could arrive this afternoon. According to the National Weather Service, a chance of showers and thunderstorms is possible this afternoon and overnight. They also say showers and thunderstorms are likely through much of the day tomorrow as well. Sunshine and cooler temperatures are forecast to return midweek, with sunny skies and highs in the low 70s through Friday. Over the weekend, Crawford County authorities reinstated the countywide burn ban as a result of ongoing dry and windy conditions.
